message.content:
Here are some of the most popular sushi restaurants in Tokyo (in no particular order):

| Restaurant | Location | Highlights |
|------------|----------|------------|
| **Sukiyabashi Jiro** | Ginza | Legendary Michelin‑starred spot famous from *Jiro Dreams of Sushi*. Requires reservations months in advance. |
| **Sushi Saito** | Ginza | Intimate 10‑seat Michelin‑starred restaurant known for impeccable precision and seasonal ingredients. |
| **Sushi Yoshitake** | Ginza | 3‑Michelin‑starred, highly exclusive, offers a refined omakase experience. |
| **Sushi Dai** | Tsukiji Outer Market | Renowned for fresh fish and long lines; a must‑visit for a classic Tsukiji sushi experience. |
| **Sushi Daiwa** | Tsukiji Outer Market | Similar to Sushi Dai but slightly less crowded; still offers top‑quality sushi. |
| **Sushi Kyubey** | Ginza | Classic, high‑end sushi with a reputation for consistency and quality. |
| **Sushi Sugita** | Ginza | Known for its “sushi of the day” concept, offering a rotating menu of fresh catches. |
| **Sushi Sawada** | Ginza | 2‑Michelin‑starred, celebrated for its meticulous preparation and seasonal focus. |
| **Sushi Masuda** | Ginza | Small, intimate setting with a focus on traditional Edomae techniques. |
| **Sushi Shikon** | Ginza | 2‑Michelin‑starred, praised for its creative yet authentic sushi offerings. |
| **Sushi Kanda** | Ginza | 3‑Michelin‑starred, offers a highly curated omakase menu with a focus on seasonal ingredients. |
| **Sushi Iwa** | Ginza | 2‑Michelin‑starred, known for its elegant presentation and high‑quality fish. |
| **Sushi Tsurutontan** | Shinjuku | A modern take on sushi with a focus on sustainability and seasonal ingredients. |
| **Sushi Noda** | Shibuya | 1‑Michelin‑starred, offers a relaxed atmosphere with a focus on fresh fish and seasonal ingredients. |
| **Sushi Saito** | Ginza | 3‑Michelin‑starred, known for its intimate setting and meticulous attention to detail. |

| **Sushi Shikon** | Ginza | 2‑Michelin‑starred, praised for its creative yet authentic sushi offerings. |
| **Sushi Kanda** | Ginza | 3‑Michelin‑starred, offers a highly curated omakase menu with a focus on seasonal ingredients. |
| **Sushi Iwa** | Ginza | 2‑Michelin‑starred, known for its elegant presentation and high‑quality fish. |
| **Sushi Tsurutontan** | Shinjuku | A modern take on sushi with a focus on sustainability and seasonal ingredients. |
| **Sushi Noda** | Shibuya | 1‑Michelin‑starred, offers a relaxed atmosphere with a focus on fresh fish and seasonal ingredients. |

These restaurants range from ultra‑exclusive Michelin‑starred spots to more accessible yet still highly regarded sushi counters. Reservations are often required, especially for the Michelin‑starred establishments, so plan ahead if you want to dine at one of these top spots.
